title: Story-state triggers: bots act as a story moves between states (M)
description:
Bots act as a story moves between states. Smallest first version: one automation fires on one state (for example copy -> copywriter), writes a new revision and moves the story on, with the idempotent claim and the hop limit. Budget and further states come after use shows what is needed.

Scope:
- An automation fires on "story entered state X".
- One claim per (story, state, revision), so runs are idempotent.
- A bot writes a new revision, then moves the story on. Wherever human input is wanted, it raises a review request (human review points story); the state itself never signals "needs a human".
- Bot transitions are labelled as bot actions.
- A per-story limit on bot hops and a per-story budget, to prevent loops.

Acceptance criteria:
- Entering the configured state starts exactly one run per (story, state, revision), even if the event is delivered twice.
- The bot's revision and transition are recorded and labelled as bot actions.
- A story exceeding its hop limit or budget stops with a review request instead of continuing.
- Bots skip stories under a group lock once the similarity story lands.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) required.

Depends on PPY-433383, the automation records story (PPY-2e6e2b) and the human review points story.
